title: Nasdaq Sets Record High as Stock Futures Edge Higher – Live Updates from CNBC
body:
Wall Street opened Tuesday on a buoyant note as equity futures nudged higher, extending the optimism that followed Monday’s historic surge in the Nasdaq Composite. The technology‑heavy index not only eclipsed its previous intraday peak but also closed at a fresh all‑time high, prompting traders to bid up futures on the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. By mid‑morning, S&P 500 futures were up roughly a quarter of a percent, while Dow futures posted modest gains, signaling that the rally could have momentum beyond a single session.

The Nasdaq’s breakthrough came after a string of earnings beats from leading chipmakers and cloud‑service providers, which helped lift the index past the 15,600‑point barrier for the first time. Analysts point to a confluence of factors: robust corporate profit reports, easing inflation expectations, and a Federal Reserve stance that appears increasingly dovish. “We’re seeing a genuine shift in market sentiment,” said Laura Chen, senior equity strategist at Meridian Capital. “Investors are finally pricing in a scenario where interest rates may stay lower for longer, which is a boon for growth‑oriented stocks that dominate the Nasdaq.”

Broader market implications are already materialising. The S&P 500, which is more diversified across sectors, has been buoyed by gains in consumer discretionary and industrial names that have benefited from a resurgence in consumer confidence. Meanwhile, the Dow, traditionally anchored by heavyweight industrials and financials, recorded a modest uptick, reflecting a more cautious but still positive tone among investors. The divergence in performance underscores how the tech rally is spilling over into the wider market, yet the degree of that spillover remains uneven.

Despite the upbeat mood, some analysts warn that the recent highs could be fragile. Valuation metrics for many technology stocks are now hovering at historic peaks, and any surprise in earnings or a shift in monetary policy could trigger a pullback. “The market is pricing in a lot of future growth,” noted Raj Patel, chief economist at Global Insight. “If the Fed signals a more aggressive tightening cycle or if macro data shows a slowdown in hiring, we could see a swift correction.” Moreover, geopolitical tensions in Eastern Europe and Asia continue to loom, adding a layer of uncertainty that could dampen investor enthusiasm.

Investors are also keeping a close eye on the upcoming earnings season, which promises a litany of reports from both tech giants and legacy manufacturers. The performance of companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Apple will be especially pivotal, as they carry significant weight in the Nasdaq’s composition. In parallel, the Federal Reserve’s next policy meeting, slated for later this month, will be scrutinized for clues about the trajectory of interest rates. A dovish tone could reinforce the current rally, while any hint of tightening may prompt a recalibration of risk appetite.

Looking ahead, the market’s trajectory will likely hinge on the interplay between corporate earnings, monetary policy, and global macro‑economic developments. If the positive earnings momentum sustains and the Fed maintains a patient approach, futures could continue to climb, potentially pushing the major indices to new milestones. Conversely, any adverse shock—be it a surprise rate hike, an earnings miss, or escalating geopolitical risk—could quickly reverse the gains. For now, the prevailing sentiment is one of cautious optimism, with traders poised to ride the wave while remaining vigilant for the next catalyst that could reshape the market’s direction.
